title: Axiomarium asset manifest
description: The asset.yaml in every asset folder: what the asset is, which harnesses it supports, what it may touch, and how far it can be trusted.

name.description: Kebab-case: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. Must match the asset's folder name.

kind.description: What the asset is. Must match its top-level folder: agents/, skills/, hooks/, policies/, workflows/ or experiments/.

version.description: The asset's own SemVer version, such as 0.1.0. Quote it if YAML would read it as a number.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the asset does.

maturity.description: How far the asset can be trusted. Each level needs the evidence registry/maturity.yaml lists.

supports.description: How well each harness is supported. List at least one.

permissions.description: What the asset is allowed to touch.

shell.description: Commands it may run: none, read-only ones such as git status, or any.

side_effects.description: The worst thing running the asset can change: nothing, something reversible, or something irreversible.

inputs.description: What the asset reads, in kebab-case words such as source-code.

outputs.description: What the asset produces, in kebab-case words such as boundary-findings.

evals.description: Which kinds of evals exist for the asset.

trigger.description: Tests that it activates when it should.

behavioral.description: Tests of what it does once active.

regression.description: Tests that guard against past failures.

support.description: full: works as intended. partial: works with gaps. experimental: unproven.
